title: Understanding the nsw paramedic salary: hourly to annual conversion guide
description: Learn how to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary for a nsw paramedic salary estimate. Includes tax, super, and fortnightly pay calculations.
salarySummary: Based on the NSW full-time ordinary time average of $2108.8 per week (38 hours), the annual equivalent is approximately $109,657.60 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly rate to an annual salary for a nsw paramedic salary?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then by 52. For a standard 38-hour week, the formula is hourly × 38 × 52. For example, $35 per hour gives $35 × 38 × 52 = $69,160 per year. This assumes no overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. Use the timesheet on this site to calculate your own figures.

faqs.q: What tax and super apply to a nsw paramedic salary?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates are: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy is generally 2%. Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. These are estimates; your actual tax may vary.

faqs.q: Does the nsw paramedic salary include casual loading?
faqs.a: The NSW full-time ordinary time average does not include casual loading. Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base rate under the National Minimum Wage and many awards. When using the timesheet, enter your base hourly rate and check the casual loading box to see the loaded rate. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the nsw paramedic salary through hourly conversion

If you are a paramedic in New South Wales or considering the role, you may want to compare an hourly rate to an annual salary. The formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. This article uses a standard 38-hour week, which is the full-time benchmark under the National Employment Standards. For a fortnightly figure, simply double the weekly amount.

### What the NSW average tells us about the nsw paramedic salary

The on-site reference shows that New South Wales full-time ordinary time earnings averaged $2108.8 per week as of May 2026. This is an average across all full-time employees in NSW, not a median for paramedics. Paramedics may earn more or less depending on their award classification, experience, and penalty rates. However, this average provides a useful benchmark. Using the formula, $2108.8 per week for 38 hours gives an annual gross of approximately $109,657.60. That figure is before tax and super.

### National Minimum Wage, award rates, and casual loading

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.9 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. Award rates for paramedics are typically higher than the minimum. The Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020 or the Ambulance and Patient Transport Industry Award may apply, but specific rates are not detailed here. Always check the relevant award or enterprise agreement for your exact pay. Superannuation is paid on top of ordinary earnings at 12%, with a maximum contribution base of $270,830.

### Tax and super considerations for your nsw paramedic salary

When converting an hourly rate to annual pay, remember that tax and super are separate. The annual gross is your hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For example, a paramedic earning $40 per hour would have an annual gross of $40 × 38 × 52 = $79,040. Fortnightly pay would be $3,040. Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates, tax on $79,040 would be approximately $14,617 plus Medicare levy of 2% ($1,580.80), leaving about $62,842 after tax. Super at 12% adds $9,484.80 on top, but that is not deducted from your pay. The [reference tables](/data) on this site provide more detailed breakdowns.

### Using the timesheet and other tools

The [timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly equivalents. A checkbox adds 25% casual loading on top of the base rate. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading. For award-specific guidance, see the [pay guides](/blog) section. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page explains the National Minimum Wage and award rates in more detail.

### Key points to remember

- The nsw paramedic salary is not a single figure; it varies by employer, experience, and conditions.
- The NSW full-time ordinary time average of $2108.8 per week is an average across all occupations, not a paramedic median.
- Always use your actual hourly rate and hours worked for a personal estimate.
- Super is paid on top of ordinary earnings, not deducted from your pay.
- Tax estimates use the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare levy uses 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here.

### Conclusion

Converting an hourly rate to an annual salary helps you compare job offers and understand your potential earnings. For a nsw paramedic salary, the average weekly earnings provide context, but your actual pay depends on your award, penalties, and overtime. Use the tools on this site to calculate your own figures, and always refer to official sources like the Fair Work Ombudsman for your specific entitlements.
